```{r}
## Loading relevant libraries
library(psych)
library(tidyverse)
library(reshape2)
library(apaTables)
library(car)

# Helper Function: Get upper triangle of the correlation matrix
get_upper_tri <- function(cormat){
    cormat[lower.tri(cormat)]<- NA
    return(cormat)
}

# Graphing functions

theme_Publication <- function(base_size=14) {
      library(grid)
      library(ggthemes)
      (theme_foundation(base_size=base_size)
       + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                         size = rel(1.2), hjust = 0.5),
               text = element_text(),
               panel.background = element_rect(colour = NA),
               plot.background = element_rect(colour = NA),
               panel.border = element_rect(colour = NA),
               axis.title = element_text(face = "bold",size = rel(1)),
               axis.title.y = element_text(angle=90,vjust =2),
               axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.2),
               axis.text = element_text(), 
               axis.line = element_line(colour="black"),
               axis.ticks = element_line(),
               panel.grid.major = element_line(colour="#f0f0f0"),
               panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
               legend.key = element_rect(colour = NA),
               legend.position = "bottom",
               legend.direction = "horizontal",
               legend.key.size= unit(0.2, "cm"),
               legend.margin = unit(0, "cm"),
               legend.title = element_text(face="italic"),
               plot.margin=unit(c(10,5,5,5),"mm"),
               strip.background=element_rect(colour="#f0f0f0",fill="#f0f0f0"),
               strip.text = element_text(face="bold")
          ))
      
}

scale_fill_Publication <- function(...){
      library(scales)
      discrete_scale("fill","Publication",manual_pal(values = c("#386cb0","#fdb462","#7fc97f","#ef3b2c","#662506","#a6cee3","#fb9a99","#984ea3","#ffff33")), ...)

}

scale_colour_Publication <- function(...){
      library(scales)
      discrete_scale("colour","Publication",manual_pal(values = c("#386cb0","#fdb462","#7fc97f","#ef3b2c","#662506","#a6cee3","#fb9a99","#984ea3","#ffff33")), ...)

}

```


```{r}
## Opening dataframe
bcpe_study1 <- 
  read_csv("/Users/luiza/Projects/ERIM/Study\ 5\ -\ Scale\ development/bcpe_study1_rep.csv") %>% 
  group_by(ID) %>% 
  mutate(bcpe = mean(
    c(
      bcpe_1, 
      bcpe_2, 
      bcpe_3, 
      bcpe_4, 
      bcpe_5, 
      bcpe_6, 
      bcpe_7, 
      bcpe_8
    ), na.rm = T)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(attention_check == 1)

```

Overall, 21 people failed a simple attention check (out of these 4 used a foreign IP Address, 7 used a VPN).

Visualizing correlation between predictors (Figure S4)

```{r}
m <- 
  bcpe_study1 %>%
  mutate(inparty_cont = ifelse(inparty == "Republican", 1, 0)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    BCPE = bcpe,
    EC = ec,
    PT = pt,
    "Theories of Empathy" = fixed_theory,
    SDO = sdo,
    SS = ss,
    PSI = psi,
    "Party Strength" = party_strength,
    "Party" = inparty_cont,
    "Ideology" = pol_id,
    TA = ta,
    NC = nc,
    "Openness" = open_general,
    Age = age,
    Gender = gender,
    Income = income,
    Education = edu,
    Animosity = animosity,
    "Social Distance" = sd,
    "Moral Disengagement" = md,
    "Bipartisan Cooperation" = coop
  ) %>% 
  drop_na()

cormat <- round(cor(m),2)
upper_tri <- get_upper_tri(cormat)
melted_cormat <- melt(upper_tri, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(melted_cormat, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value))+
  geom_tile(color = "white")+
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "darkgreen", high = "darkblue", mid = "white", 
                       midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1,1), space = "Lab", 
                       name="Pearson\nCorrelation") +
  theme_Publication()+ # minimal theme
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, 
                                   size = 12, hjust = 1))+
  coord_fixed() +
  geom_text(aes(Var2, Var1, label = value), color = "black", size = 4) +
  theme(
  axis.title.x = element_blank(),
  axis.title.y = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
  panel.border = element_blank(),
  panel.background = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank(),
  legend.justification = c(1, 0),
  legend.position = c(0.6, 0.7),
  legend.direction = "horizontal") +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 7, barheight = 1,
                title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

```

## Model Comparisons: Does BCPE uniquely predict measures of partisan division? (Table 1)

```{r}

# Desire for Bipartisan Cooperation
model_aug1 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(bcpe)
            + scale(open_general)
            + scale(ec) 
            + scale(pt) 
            + scale(fixed_theory) 
            + scale(ss) 
            + scale(sdo) 
            + scale(ta) 
            + scale(nc)
            + scale(psi)
            + scale(age)
            + gender
            + scale(income)
            + scale(edu)
            + scale(pol_id)
            + scale(party_strength)
            + inparty, bcpe_study1)
summary(model_aug1)
## Testing the augmented model for multicollinearity
vif(model_aug1)

model_small1 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(open_general)
            + scale(ec) 
            + scale(pt) 
            + scale(fixed_theory) 
            + scale(ss) 
            + scale(sdo) 
            + scale(ta) 
            + scale(nc)
            + scale(psi)
            + scale(age)
            + gender
            + scale(income)
            + scale(edu)
            + scale(pol_id)
            + scale(party_strength)
            + inparty, bcpe_study1) 

anova(model_small1, model_aug1)
### Calculating r square change
summary(model_aug1)$r.squared - summary(model_small1)$r.squared

##Getting confidence intervals 
exp(cbind(coef(model_aug1), confint(model_aug1)))

## Animosity

model_aug1 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(bcpe)
            + scale(open_general)
            + scale(ec) 
            + scale(pt) 
            + scale(fixed_theory) 
            + scale(ss)

            + gender
            + scale(income)
            + scale(edu)
            + scale(pol_id)
            + scale(party_strength)
            + inparty, bcpe_study1)
summary(model_aug1)
vif(model_aug1)

model_small1 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(open_general)

### Calculating r square change

##Getting confidence intervals

anova(model_small1, model_aug1)
```

```{r}
## Interactions

model2 <- lm(scale(sd) ~ scale(bcpe)*inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(sd) ~ scale(bcpe) + inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(bcpe)*inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(bcpe) + inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(bcpe)*inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(bcpe) + inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(md) ~ scale(bcpe)*inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(md) ~ scale(bcpe) + inparty, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(md) ~ scale(bcpe)*party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(md) ~ scale(bcpe) + party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(sd) ~ scale(bcpe)*party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(sd) ~ scale(bcpe) + party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(bcpe)*party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(animosity) ~ scale(bcpe) + party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)

model2 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(bcpe)*party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
model1 <- lm(scale(coop) ~ scale(bcpe) + party_strength, data = bcpe_study1)
anova(model1, model2)


```

Graphing the relationship between BCPE and measures of partisan division (Figure S3)

```{r}
cor.test(bcpe_study1$bcpe, bcpe_study1$md)
bcpe_study1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(bcpe, md)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = c(1:7)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  annotate("text", x = 15, y = 1.5, label = "r = -.45, p < .001", color = "blue", size = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Beliefs in Cross-Partisan Empathy\n(greater value = more positive beliefs)",
       y = "Moral Disengagement") +
  theme_Publication()

cor.test(bcpe_study1$bcpe, bcpe_study1$coop)
bcpe_study1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(bcpe, coop)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 5), breaks = c(1:5)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  annotate("text", x = 85, y = 1.5, label = "r = .28, p < .001", color = "blue", size = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Beliefs in Cross-Partisan Empathy\n(greater value = more positive beliefs)",
       y = "Desire for Bipartisan Cooperation") +
  theme_Publication()

cor.test(bcpe_study1$bcpe, bcpe_study1$animosity)
bcpe_study1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(bcpe, animosity)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  annotate("text", x = 85, y = 10, label = "r = -.25, p < .001", color = "blue", size = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Beliefs in Cross-Partisan Empathy\n(greater value = more positive beliefs)",
       y = "Partisan Animosity") +
  theme_Publication()
cor.test(bcpe_study1$bcpe, bcpe_study1$sd)

bcpe_study1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(bcpe, sd)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = c(1:7)) +
  annotate("text", x = 15, y = 1.5, label = "r = -0.35, p < .001", color = "blue", size = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Beliefs in Cross-Partisan Empathy\n(greater value = more positive beliefs)",
       y = "Desire for Social Distance") +
  theme_Publication()

```
